paper_name: Unsqueeze [CLS] Bottleneck to Learn Rich Representations

sections.abstract: Distillation-based self-supervised learning (SSL) often results in over-compressed representations due to radical clustering and sharp target distributions. To address this, the authors introduce UDI (Unsqueezed Distillation-based SSL), which enriches learned representations by encouraging multimodal predictions distilled from a consolidated profile of local predictions derived via stratified sampling. Evaluations demonstrate that UDI promotes semantically meaningful representations at the instance level, achieving superior or competitive results in image classification and significant improvements in dense prediction tasks like object detection and segmentation. UDI also performs well in low-shot image classification, enhancing the scalability of joint-embedding pipelines. Source code is available at https://github.com/ISL-CV/udi.
sections.introduction: Self-supervised learning (SSL) aims to understand visual data's intrinsic properties without explicit labels. While methods like DINOv2, MoCov3, and iBOT capture a spectrum of information, they often fall short of capturing comprehensive image information. Implicit clustering (e.g., SimCLR, VICReg) can lead to weak compression and overfitting, while explicit clustering (e.g., DINO, iBOT) can cause over-compression and loss of meaningful nuisances due to skewed sharpening. Issues like semantic misalignment and enforced alignment across different levels further limit performance. UDI is proposed to overcome these by identifying constraints through the lens of Multiview Information Bottleneck (MIB) and adopting self-distillation across levels. It extracts patch-level representations via an extra self-attention (SA) update, functioning as soft-masked pooling to align semantic types. The key contribution is a novel objective combining predictions from different levels to construct a multi-modal target distribution, infusing 'meaningful nuisances' into the representation. UDI achieves 77.6% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K with a linear classifier and 75.6% with a k-NN classifier, showing strong performance in low-shot learning and dense prediction tasks.
sections.related work: The paper reviews SSL with distillation, noting that works like DINO cast knowledge distillation as a self-supervised objective with an online teacher model. Subsequent works like iBOT and DINOv2 integrate Masked Image Modeling (MIM) to factor in finer granularity. Multi-level clustering approaches (e.g., EsViT, DINO+SelfPatch, CrOC) have improved dense prediction but lack in-depth analysis of synergistic interactions between objectives. UDI aims to fill this gap by analyzing these interactions through the MIB framework.
sections.methodology: UDI is framed within multiview information bottleneck (MIB) learning, where the objective is upper-bounded by: \\mathcal{L}_{MIB} = -I(\\mathbf{y};\\mathbf{y}') + \\beta D_{\\text{SKL}}[P(\\mathbf{y} \\mid \\mathbf{x})||P(\\mathbf{y}' \\mid \\mathbf{x}')] (Eq 1). UDI adopts the DINO objective for both image and patch levels: \\mathcal{L}_{image} = \\mathcal{L}_{cls} = \\mathbb{E}_{\\mathbf{z}_{cls},\\mathbf{z}'_{cls}\\in \\mathcal{Z}_{cls}}[\\text{H}(p_t(y|\\mathbf{z}'_{cls}), p_s(y|\\mathbf{z}_{cls}))] and \\mathcal{L}_{patch} = \\mathbb{E}_{\\mathbf{z}_p,\\mathbf{z}'_p\\in \\mathcal{Z}_p}[\\text{H}(p_t(y|\\mathbf{z}'_p), p_s(y|\\mathbf{z}_p))] (Eq 2). To align semantics, patch-level representations are extracted via a self-attention (SA) update: \\hat{\\mathbf{z}}_i = \\text{SA}(\\mathbf{z}_i, \\mathbf{Z}, \\mathbf{Z}) = \\mathbf{W}_V\\mathbf{Z} \\text{softmax}(\\frac{1}{\\tau}\\mathbf{Z}^{\\top}(\\mathbf{W}_K^\\top \\mathbf{W}_Q)\\mathbf{z}_i) (Eq 4). To prevent over-compression, UDI constructs a multi-modal target distribution by modeling an image as a mixture of semantic concepts: p(y|\\mathbf{Z}) \\approx \\frac{1}{M}\\sum_{i=1}^{M}p(y|\\hat{\\mathbf{z}}_i) (Eq 6), using stratified random sampling. This is blended with the regular class token prediction: p^*(y|\\mathbf{Z}) = \\alpha p(y|\\mathbf{Z}) + (1-\\alpha) p(y|\\mathbf{z}_{cls}) (Eq 7). An extra class token \\mathbf{z}_{cls+} is learned via: \\mathcal{L}_{cls+} = \\mathbb{E}_{\\mathbf{Z}'\\in \\mathcal{Z},\\mathbf{z}_{cls+}\\in \\mathcal{Z}_{cls+}}[\\text{H}(p^*_t(y|\\mathbf{Z}'), p_s(y|\\mathbf{z}_{cls+}))] (Eq 8). This 'unsqueezes' the bottleneck, improving Forman curvature. The total loss is \\mathcal{L}_{UDI} = \\mathcal{L}_{image} + \\mathcal{L}_{patch} = \\mathcal{L}_{cls} + \\mathcal{L}_{cls+} + \\mathcal{L}_{patch} (Eq 11).
sections.experiments: Experiments use ViT-S/16 pretrained on ImageNet-1K for 300 epochs. UDI achieves 77.6% linear probing top-1 accuracy and 75.6% k-NN accuracy, outperforming DINO and iBOT. In low-shot learning, UDI reaches 66.7% accuracy with 1% labels. For downstream tasks, UDI shows superior performance in object detection and instance segmentation on COCO (43.2 \\(AP^{bb}\\), 39.4 \\(AP^{mk}\\)) and semantic segmentation on ADE20K (43.7 mIoU with UperNet). Video object segmentation on DAVIS-2017 also shows gains (62.9 \\(\mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F}_m\\)). Ablation studies confirm that UDI's soft-masked pooling via SA is more effective than similarity or position-based constraints. The shared projector and multimodal objective \\mathcal{L}_{cls+} significantly contribute to performance, with a blending factor \\alpha=0.5 being optimal.
sections.conclusion: UDI addresses information compression issues in SSL by introducing a multi-level approach with context-aligned semantic constraints, semantic-type-aligned objectives via a shared projector, and an extra class token for multimodal predictions. Extensive experiments demonstrate its effectiveness in both classification and dense prediction tasks. Limitations include a current focus on ViT-S/16, with future work planned for non-ViT backbones and larger models.
sections.supplementary: The supplementary material provides an in-depth review of SSL via implicit (contrastive and non-contrastive) and explicit clustering (DeepCluster, SwAV, MSN, DINO). It details multi-level SSL methods like DenseCL, PixPro, and iBOT. PyTorch-like pseudocode for the UDI framework is provided in Algorithm 1. Implementation details cover data augmentation (BYOL/DINO style), multi-crop settings (2 global, 10 local crops), and pretraining hyperparameters (AdamW, cosine schedule, linear scaling rule). Training costs for UDI are shown to be similar to iBOT. Additional results include a comprehensive comparison of multi-level objectives, showing UDI achieves the best trade-off between classification and detection. Ablations on the stratified random sampling window size show that a 3x3 grid is optimal. An experiment with a complete MIB objective (combining InfoNCE and DINO) shows that UDI's approach is more effective at preserving nuisances. Extensive attention visualizations (Figs 1.1-1.3) illustrate that UDI's standard class token \\mathbf{z}_{cls} focuses on foreground objects while the extra token \\mathbf{z}_{cls+} captures both foreground and background details, reflecting the image's semantic composition.
